plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Reduce CRWD to 10% to further diversify single name exposure.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets capital preservation with a potential ~1.5%/month return. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest growth.

balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for risk-first growth, targeting around ~2.5%/month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad market exposure with quality tech. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns.

plan: Increase SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 6% to lean into leveraged ETFs, staying within the combined limit.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets stretch growth, aiming for ~4%/month, but comes with significantly higher risk. It uses leverage and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be prepared for larger drawdowns and be aware of leveraged ETF decay and daily rebalancing; strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, CRWD, and SMH to near zero to eliminate high-beta and leveraged exposure.
Increase QQQI to 30% to prioritize income and broad market exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and maintain a cash-like position.
Buy JEPQ at 10% to add another income-focused ETF for monthly distributions.
income.read: This income plan focuses on parking cash for yield, targeting around ~1%/month in distributions. It significantly reduces growth-oriented holdings and leverage for lower drawdown. Remember, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in market selloffs.
